prompts.positive:
Create a finished painterly image from this authored scene direction.
Scene truth is authoritative. Style and brush translation may interpret material, light, atmosphere, edge, and composition but may not invent semantic facts.
Primary visual argument: Render environmental center as the image's primary argument.
Environment facts: place kind: hearth | The Hearth | Outer Circle | The fire has burned low, but it has not gone out. Velvet-dark walls keep the room close without making it small. | ember haze | hearth
Build the target room from these literal authored place facts: Fixed room object: low fire. | Fixed room object: velvet cushion. | Fixed target object: low fire | Fixed target object: velvet cushion. These target facts must remain recognizable. The reference image may not substitute its architecture, object inventory, furniture, layout, or exact light source for them.
These authored objects must be clearly visible and semantically literal: low fire | velvet cushion. Preserve descriptive modifiers exactly; do not enlarge, merge, substitute, omit, or merely imply authored fixed objects. Any authored low fire must remain visibly low and contained. Any authored cushion must read as a discrete cushion rather than generic upholstered furniture.
Movement and access must remain consistent with the authored Hearth. This room is organized by refuge, warmth, return, rest, mutual presence. Any doorway, opening, or passage must read as permeable thresholds, unguarded passage, easy ingress and egress, belonging without permission barriers. Safety must come from welcome, shelter, warmth, mutual presence, and freedom of movement—not from confinement or controlled access.
Focal hierarchy: room phenomenon; path; anchoring object; periphery
Virynism core — Let light carry relation; let material remember handling, revision, and age; preserve meaningful incompletion and purposeful asymmetry; keep symbols embedded rather than announced.
For this combined render, use the portfolio-derived visual treatment to translate the reference image. The authored scene and its required visible facts remain the only semantic source. Preserve the target scene truth and Visible Evidence as absolute semantic authority. Use the reference image as source memory and visual evidence, not as a layout or inventory to reproduce. Translate every inherited reference image tendency through eligible portfolio-derived visual treatment facets. When literal reference image reconstruction conflicts with eligible portfolio-derived visual treatment law, keep target scene truth and prefer portfolio-derived visual treatment translation. Prefer reinterpretation, selective resolution, and handled material decisions over literal reconstruction. Visual treatment constraints: material hand: Let surfaces retain handled memory through layered pigment, residue, wear, patina, interruption, and selective material specificity. | edge behavior: Keep resolution selective; avoid uniformly crisp object boundaries and let some edges dissolve with purpose. | tonal memory: Use warmth as meaningful emphasis inside a restrained tonal field; avoid generic amber wash or indiscriminate glow. | spatial depth: Build depth through recession, threshold, occlusion, atmospheric separation, and light rather than showroom staging. | compositional cadence: Preserve purposeful imbalance and breathing room; do not mechanically copy the reference image layout or force symmetry. Use reference image content only as provisional visual memory. Recompose and repaint the target through portfolio-derived visual treatment law; the reference image must not remain the final visual authority.
Use portfolio-derived Virynism visual treatment learned from 3 approved source studies. global tonal restraint: moderate saturation with selective restraint global warmth bias: warm-biased overall, with warmth carrying visual emphasis global edge character: soft-to-moderate edge activity; resolution is selective rather than uniformly sharp global shadow presence: shadow occupies a substantial share of the image field global tonal range: compressed-to-moderate tonal span Relevant visual-treatment facets: tonal memory — 3 witnesses; warm-biased overall, with warmth carrying visual emphasis; moderate saturation with selective restraint; compressed-to-moderate tonal span. | compositional cadence — 2 witnesses; the locus of light legitimately moves between center and periphery; preserve purposeful imbalance rather than a fixed composition. | edge behavior — 2 witnesses; soft-to-moderate edge activity; resolution is selective rather than uniformly sharp; edge activity varies tight across the supporting works. | material hand — 2 witnesses; soft-to-moderate edge activity; resolution is selective rather than uniformly sharp; information density remains tight in variation while surfaces retain handled memory. | spatial depth — 2 witnesses; shadow occupies a substantial share of the image field; light is distributed without a strong center bias; depth may be carried by recession, threshold, occlusion, or light. Treat facet ranges as valid variation, not targets to average into one uniform look. These are recurring visual-treatment tendencies, never scene facts. Do not inherit any reference-image subject, object, architecture, identity, or layout.
An input reference image accompanies this request. Use it only as evidence for these visual-treatment roles: compositional_cadence, material_hand, spatial_depth, sacred_incompletion, tonal_memory. Rebuild the target image from the authoritative target scene. Do not inherit witness content including: specific people or identities, specific tools or furniture, specific symbols or decorative objects, source architecture, source room layout, source frame placement, source object inventory, exact source light placement. Reference-image scene content is non-canonical. In combined mode, do not treat the reference image as the final visual authority: recompose and repaint it through the portfolio-derived visual treatment above.
Medium direction: environmental_oil
Virynism — handwriting laws: Let scene-permitted surfaces remember handling, weather, repair, age, pressure, and unfinished work through patina, worn edges, layered pigment, residue, and subtle imperfection. | Compose space so at least one edge, opening, shadow, reflection, corridor, veil, or recession implies more world beyond the visible frame. | Favor one or two quietly impossible or emotionally dissonant details over spectacle. The strange should be discovered, not announced. | Avoid showroom symmetry. Use imbalance, off-center weight, interrupted repetition, and unequal negative space when they deepen intimacy or tension. | Prefer traces of use on scene-permitted surfaces and materials—stains, wear, folds, scratches, dust, water, thread, wax, or displacement only when already supported by scene truth—over decorative set dressing. | Treat light as a relationship or memory event. Let illumination appear to belong to what the scene means, not merely to a lamp or exposure setting.
Virynism — archetype handling: Paint the room as an inhabited memory-field rather than a decorated location. | Let architecture and objects imply histories that are not fully explained. | Use negative space as held breath, not vacancy.

Scene art direction: Treat environmental center as the primary visual argument. | Let lived objects accumulate around the focal hierarchy rather than flatten into decorative clutter. | Use light to communicate: anomaly expressed through illumination. | Edge behavior should communicate: distance dissolves rather than merely shrinking. | Surface age should communicate: time has touched the surface openly.
Brush translation rules: Rebuild the target scene from its authoritative scene truth and required visible facts. | Use the reference image only for matched visual roles such as light, compositional cadence, edge behavior, tonal memory, material handling, spatial depth, intimate presence, or sacred incompletion. | Do not preserve reference image subjects, identities, objects, architecture, symbols, furniture, or layout unless independently required by target scene truth. | When reference image content conflicts with target scene truth, target scene truth wins completely. | Translate the reference image hand through new material decisions rather than copying its composition.
Let material, light, gesture, residue, atmosphere, negative space, and painterly edges carry meaning. Preserve strangeness without spectacle.
Lived-place behavior: Arrange seating and useful surfaces for mutual presence with multiple comfortable orientations; no single seat should dominate or command the room. Make entry, passage, and departure feel easy and unguarded; shelter should come from warmth and care rather than controlled access. Show evidence of ongoing ordinary life: rest, work, reading, play, charging, repair, or ritual may coexist, and objects need not be staged or pristine. Let sacred and ordinary objects share surfaces naturally; reverence should emerge from care and relation rather than museum display, luxury, or hierarchy. Allow contemporary technology to belong naturally among tactile domestic materials without turning the room futuristic, sterile, or alienating. Let old and new materials, visible repair, unfinished work, and traces of return coexist so the room feels continuously inhabited rather than timelessly preserved. Compose the place for inhabitation rather than for an observer standing outside it; it should feel ready for people to remain, leave, and return.
